text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- At the beginning of March this year, 29 percent of Poles were ready to vote for Solidarity Electoral Action (AWS) in the upcoming parliamentary elections, 26 percent supported the ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD), 12 percent favoured the Polish Peasant Party (PSL) and 12 percent supported the centrist Union for Freedom (UW), a survey by the PBS polling institute said.
- The nationalist rightwing KPN-OP political party, which has joined the opposition Solidarity Electoral Action, wants the Solidarity coalition to register as a political party in two months time.
KPN-OP is also planning to propose a law allowing the investigation of the legality of property acquistion by people who became rich after 1989, KPN-OP leader Adam Slomka said.

- The Polish fishing trawler Aquarius has not yet been released from the Russian port of Petropavlosk following its arrest in the Sea of Okhotsk by the Russian coast guard for allegedly fishing without permission.
NOWA EUROPA

- The opposition centrist Union for Freedom (UW) and the centrist Stronnictwo Demokratyczne democratic alliance will stand together in the parliamentatry elections later this year, the two parties said.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET STORIES
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- The state treasury and the Banking Guarantee Fund (BFG) provided Poland's ailing banks 1.38 billion zlotys last year.

- Revenues from privatisation of Poland's "family jewels" -- large firms such as the CPN petrol distribution chain, telecom monopolist TPSA, copper combine KGHM, Bank Handlowy, LOT Polish Airlines and the Petrochemia Plock oil refinery -- will most likely go to old-age pension funds to be created from the revamp of the country's social security system, the government said.

- If Poland's harvests are good this summer and petroleum producers do not raise fuel prices again, year-on-year inflation will not exceed 14 percent, the finance ministry's economic research institute said.
- The Kalisz-based Wistil polyester textile maker is planning to double its output and sales in up to three years time following plant modernisation, company president Andrzej Urbaniak said.
Wistil will list its shares on the Warsaw bourse in the fourth quarter of this year.
- The Hellena carbonated drink and juice maker produced 105 million litres of drinks last year and 16.5 million litres of juice.
In January 1997 the firm's sales soared by 190 percent compared with the same period the year before and by 235 percent in February, the company said.
NOWA EUROPA
- Around 40 cosmetics makers exhibited their products in the Estetyka '97 cosmetics exhibition in Warsaw last week.
- The times of a centrally steered economy are over in Poland as the result of the government's administrative reform, economy minister Wieslaw Kaczmarek said.
The present foreign trade deficit is a natural consequence of economic development, Kaczmarek said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- A Polish-language edition of the Cosmopolitan women's magazine will be issued in May this year.
The magazine, to cost 4.9 zlotys, will start with a print run of 200,000 copies.
ZYCIE

- The Hetman National Investment Fund (NFI) No. 15 has not yet sold any of the companies it controls. The fund is planning corporate sales in the future after it carries out restructuring and modernisation of the companies, which will enable it to get the best price for sold firms, fund managing firm president Krzysztof Sedzikowski said.
